title: Anaphylaxis (Adult)
indications: Suspected anaphylaxis: rash/hives + respiratory distress or hypotension after allergen exposure.
steps: Administer epinephrine 0.3-0.5 mg IM (1:1000), lateral thigh.
High-flow oxygen, position of comfort or supine if hypotensive.
IV access, consider fluid bolus if hypotensive.
Administer diphenhydramine 25-50 mg IV/IM if available.
Repeat epinephrine q5-15min if no improvement.
Transport, consider ALS intercept if BLS.
reference_note: SEED/DEMO protocol only -- replace with your agency's actual medical-direction-approved protocols before any real use. The 'symptoms' and 'synonyms' lists are retrieval aids for matching how an EMT phrases a query; they are NOT diagnostic criteria and must not be presented as such.

title: Suspected Opioid Overdose
indications: Respiratory depression/apnea with suspected opioid use (pinpoint pupils, track marks, scene evidence).
steps: Support airway/ventilation first -- BVM as needed.
Re-assess respiratory rate q2-3min, repeat naloxone as needed.
Be prepared for combative patient on reversal -- opioid withdrawal.
Transport; do not leave scene even if patient refuses after reversal.

title: Chest Pain / Suspected ACS
steps: 12-lead ECG as soon as possible, transmit to receiving facility if capable.
Aspirin 162-325 mg PO chewed if no contraindication.
Nitroglycerin per local protocol if SBP > 100 and no PDE5 inhibitor use.
Transport to PCI-capable facility if STEMI criteria met.
